speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to better understand this, how long has it been present and did it start as a blister or a cut?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

The history of a rapidly enlarging, painful ulcer on the leg starting at a minor trauma (ant bite) in a patient with Crohn's disease, diabetes, and a history of uveitis is highly characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum. I do not require further testing at this time to confirm this clinical diagnosis.
